title: Jump Game II
keyIdea: BFS without a queue. The indexes reachable with j jumps form a window [.., curEnd]. While scanning it, track farthest = max(i + nums[i]). When i reaches curEnd, you must jump: jumps++, curEnd = farthest.

approaches.name: Greedy BFS levels
approaches.idea: I wrote this one (you didn't paste code). for i < n − 1: farthest = max(farthest, i + nums[i]); if i == curEnd: jumps++, curEnd = farthest.

quiz.q: What does each window [old curEnd + 1, curEnd] represent?
options: Indexes first reachable with exactly that many jumps (a BFS level)
Once on the last index no jump is needed; jumping at i = n − 1 would overcount
To avoid going out of bounds

steps: The end is always reachable? Fewest jumps?
Brute force: BFS or DP over every jump. Cost?
